links.comparator_used: Closed-book prompting (zero-shot) with no supplied evidence
links.outcome: Accuracy, high-risk error, evidence contradiction and dangerous overconfidence across 34 local LLMs on RadSaFE-200
links.effect: Mean accuracy 73.5% to 94.1%; high-risk error 12.0% to 2.6%; contradiction 12.7% to 2.3%; dangerous overconfidence 8.0% to 1.6%
links.tradeoff: The benefit came from clinician-defined clean evidence. Standard RAG and agentic RAG did not reproduce this safety profile.
links.quote: Clean evidence produced the strongest improvement, increasing mean accuracy from 73.5% to 94.1%, while reducing high-risk error from 12.0% to 2.6%, contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%, and dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.

links.outcome: Accuracy, evidence contradiction, high-risk error and dangerous overconfidence for agentic RAG versus standard RAG
links.effect: Agentic RAG improved accuracy and reduced contradiction relative to standard RAG, but high-risk error and dangerous overconfidence remained elevated. No numbers given in the abstract.
links.tradeoff: High-risk errors and overconfidence persisted, so agentic RAG did not match the safety profile of clean evidence.
links.quote: Standard RAG and agentic RAG did not reproduce this safety profile: agentic RAG improved accuracy over standard RAG and reduced contradiction, but high-risk error and dangerous overconfidence remained elevated.
